newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-National Foods sees higher yr net.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-National Foods sees higher yr net.

text.p: National Foods Ltd said on Tuesday it saw a strong improvement in net profit before abnormals in the year to June 30, 1997.

"Directors are forecasting improved earnings for both milk beverages and dairy foods for the remainder of this financial year, which should lead to a strong improvement in the net profit after tax (before abnormals) for the full year," National Foods said in its first half profit results statement.
Earlier National Foods reported a half year net loss of A$12.31 million, compared with a A$7.42 million profit in the same period a year earlier.
The result included a pre-tax abnormal loss of A$36.25 million, up from a A$4.02 million abnormal loss in the first half of 1995/96.
The abnormal related to expenses from a group restructuring.
National Foods' first half net profit before abnormals rose 17 percent to A$13.4 million.
Group sales rose seven percent to A$613 million.
Earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) for the half rose to A$28.9 million for the half year from A$27.6 million, including earnings from the recently sold NationalPak unit.
Once NationalPak's earnings are taken out, EBIT rose 12 percent to A$20.1 million.

National Foods held its interim dividend steady at three cents per share. EBIT from the group's milk products division rose to A$20.7 million from A$14.1 million, while Juice EBIT fell to A$0.9 million from A$2.1 million.
Dairy foods EBIT fell to A$0.7 million from A$4.0 million.
"Milk beverages achieved significantly higher results supported by continued success of flavoured and modified milk roducts and improved margins," National Foods said.
"Juice business was successful in retaining its market segment share, however a decline in the total market led to a four percent fall in sales," it said.

"Dairy Foods' result reflects the reduced market share...following a significant new entrant into the yogurt and dairy desserts market, and the increased competitive nature of the market as all participants pursued volume growth and market share."
National Foods said it expected milk product margins to show limited growth.

"Whole milk volumes are likely to remain static or to incur a slight decline, however flavoured and modified milks particularly the comapany's Classica and I.S. brands, should continue to increase volumes," it said.

The total juice market was likely to remain static at best, while the dairy foods unit was in a strong position because of the improved market share of Yoplait and a relaunch of its Fruche fruit yoghurt product, it said.
National Foods posted a net profit before abnormals of A$22.7 million in 1995/96, up from A$19.2 million in 1994/95.
National Foods' share price was unchanged at A$1.50 at 3.10 p.m. (0410 GMT)
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
